title: 11th Word: Introduction to the Parable and the Sultan's Purpose

questions.question: What does the passage ask the reader to think about at the beginning?
questions.answer: It asks the reader to think about a short example that helps explain why the world exists, why human beings were created, and the secret of the daily prayers.

questions.question: Who is the main person in the comparison?
questions.answer: A powerful king.

questions.question: What kinds of things did the king own?
questions.answer: He owned great treasures, hidden riches, amazing skills, deep knowledge, and many kinds of learning.

questions.question: Why did the king want to open a display?
questions.answer: He wanted to show his beauty, excellence, power, wealth, art, and knowledge.

questions.question: What is the first way the king wanted to see his own perfection?
questions.answer: He wanted to see it himself directly.

questions.question: What is the second way the king wanted to see his own perfection?
questions.answer: He wanted to see it through how others looked at it.

questions.question: What does the king’s wish to display his treasures and skills tell us about him?
questions.answer: It shows that he wanted what was inside him to become known and seen.

questions.question: Which is more than money in the king’s possessions: only jewels, or jewels plus knowledge and skill?
questions.answer: Jewels plus knowledge and skill.

questions.question: How do we know the king was not ordinary?
questions.answer: He had many treasures, hidden wonders, unusual arts, and wide knowledge.

questions.question: What big idea ties the whole passage together?
questions.answer: A being with great beauty and perfection wants those qualities to be seen and known.

questions.question: What title is given at the start of the marked passage?
questions.answer: The Eleventh Word.

questions.question: What holy words come before the explanation begins?
questions.answer: The passage begins in the name of Allah and then gives verses that point to signs in creation.

questions.question: Name three things from creation mentioned in the verses.
questions.answer: The sun, the moon, and the earth.

questions.question: What human part is mentioned along with the sky and the earth?
questions.answer: The self, or soul.

questions.question: After the verses, what does the reader get invited to do?
questions.answer: To reflect on a brief comparison.

questions.question: What subjects does that comparison help explain?
questions.answer: The purpose of the world, the creation of human beings, and the meaning of the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: In the comparison, what did the king have besides visible treasures?
questions.answer: He also had hidden treasures and inner excellences like skill and knowledge.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that people with beauty and perfection want to see and show it?
questions.answer: To help explain why the king wanted to prepare a public display.

questions.question: What did the king hope people would notice in his display?
questions.answer: His rule, wealth, artistic skill, and knowledge.

questions.question: What lesson can a student infer from the two “respects” mentioned at the end?
questions.answer: Goodness and beauty can be appreciated personally and also recognized through the understanding of others.

questions.question: What kind of example is used to teach the lesson in this passage?
questions.answer: A story-like comparison about a king.

questions.question: What was special about the king’s stored wealth?
questions.answer: It included many precious gems and other hidden wonders.

questions.question: What else made the king great besides wealth?
questions.answer: His mastery in arts, his broad knowledge, and his deep learning.

questions.question: What did the king prepare so people could see what he had?
questions.answer: A place of display, like an exhibition.

questions.question: What was the purpose of making that display?
questions.answer: To make his greatness and qualities visible.

questions.question: According to the passage, why is it natural for such a king to do that?
questions.answer: Because one who has beauty and perfection wants to see it and show it.

questions.question: What does “majesty of his rule” point to in simple words?
questions.answer: His greatness as a ruler and the strength of his authority.

questions.question: Did the king want the display only for himself, or also for others?
questions.answer: For himself and for others.

questions.question: How can we tell the king’s knowledge was very wide?
questions.answer: The passage says he knew many amazing sciences and many branches of learning.

questions.question: What is one main message from the ending of the marked passage?
questions.answer: The king wanted his perfection to be witnessed in two ways: by himself and by others.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to with the word “Brother”?
questions.answer: The reader or listener.

questions.question: What does the phrase about “my own nafs” show?
questions.answer: It shows the speaker is also reflecting on himself, not only teaching others.

questions.question: In the story, what did the king have that was hidden from people at first?
questions.answer: Secret treasures and wondrous riches.

questions.question: What kind of abilities did the king have in addition to possessions?
questions.answer: Excellent artistic ability and great knowledge.

questions.question: Why was the king’s display not just about showing riches?
questions.answer: Because he also wanted to show his wisdom, art, and perfection.

questions.question: What are the two ways the king wanted to observe his beauty and perfection?
questions.answer: By seeing them himself and by seeing them through others.

questions.question: Which part of the passage helps explain the reason for making the display: the list of treasures, or the two “respects” at the end?
questions.answer: The two “respects” at the end explain the reason most clearly.

questions.question: What is the best short summary of the marked passage?
questions.answer: It tells of a king with great riches and perfection who wants those qualities to be seen directly and through the view of others.

questions.question: What Qur’anic signs are mentioned before the story starts?
questions.answer: Signs like the sun, moon, day, night, sky, earth, and the human self.

questions.question: Why are these signs mentioned before the comparison?
questions.answer: They prepare the reader to think about creation and its meaning.

questions.question: What kind of king is described in the comparison?
questions.answer: A king with huge wealth, rare treasures, great skill, and deep knowledge.

questions.question: What precious items are named among his treasures?
questions.answer: Diamonds, emeralds, and other jewels.

questions.question: What does the passage say about his learning?
questions.answer: It was broad, deep, and covered many difficult subjects.

questions.question: What moved the king to set up a display?
questions.answer: His wish to reveal and witness his beauty and perfection.

questions.question: What four things did he especially want people to see in the display?
questions.answer: His authority, wealth, art, and knowledge.

questions.question: How many main ways of seeing his perfection are mentioned?
questions.answer: Two.

questions.question: What is the difference between those two ways?
questions.answer: One is his own direct seeing, and the other is seeing it reflected in others’ view.

questions.question: If a student says, “The king only wanted praise,” what part of the passage corrects that idea?
questions.answer: The part showing he also wanted to behold his perfection himself, not only have others look at it.

questions.question: What does the marked passage begin with before the story of the king?
questions.answer: It begins with sacred opening words and verses about signs in creation.

questions.question: What lesson is the reader told he may understand a little better through the comparison?
questions.answer: He may understand the purpose of the world, the creation of people, and the mystery of the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: In the story, what did the king own in very large amounts?
questions.answer: Precious treasures and many kinds of riches.

questions.question: What “hidden” things did the king have that were not simple objects?
questions.answer: Secret treasures, special arts, and knowledge.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect beauty and perfection with wanting to display them?
questions.answer: Because it presents that desire as something natural.

questions.question: What did the king decide to open up?
questions.answer: A public showing or exhibition.

questions.question: For whose view was the display prepared?
questions.answer: For the people, and also for the king himself in another way.

questions.question: What two qualities of the king are shown by his wanting others to see his art and knowledge?
questions.answer: His excellence and his wish to make it known.

questions.question: Is the passage mainly about building something, or about the reason for showing perfection?
questions.answer: It is mainly about the reason for showing perfection.

questions.question: What is a strong main idea a 5th-grade student should remember from this passage?
questions.answer: Great beauty, knowledge, and perfection are meant to be recognized and appreciated.
